title: Playing on the coastwise steamer with Freida Shaw
summary: Joe sailed San Pedro to Seattle on a converted destroyer, playing meals and dances for twenty-five dollars a week plus room and board, and bootlegged on the side.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: I went on a boat... This was a coastwide steamer, they called it at the time.
It went up and down the California coast?
It went from San Pedro to Wilmington (that is where the boats docked) to Seattle.
Oh, it went a good way, then.
Yes. It was the fastest coastwise steamer in the world at the time. It was a converted destroyer that was made into an ocean liner.
From World War One?
Yes.
You called these coastwide steamers?

Coastwide, that went up and down one coast. Their schedule was the Pacific Coast from Wilmington to Seattle. I think once in a while it went up to Vancouver. Well, you know, the schedules on boats. We used to have to play for lunch, and we'd play for when passengers
Darensbourg - 182
boarded the ship, and we'd play for a dance.
And this girl's band...
Freida Shaw.
It was under her name?

Yes. Freida Shaw and Band. Earl Thompson, and we had a violin player named Wilma Bratton. She was a good violin player. But like I said, that was our schedule. We got $25 a week, $100 a month. They paid off every two weeks.
But you had your room and board.
Room and board, and laundry.
So you were quite a bit better off than when you were with Mutt and them, doing the taxi dances.
Plus tips, and a little bootlegging that I did.
On the boat?
Yes. They had a second cook named Nidro that I had... On my first trip I met him in Seattle. We had overnight in Seattle, and we would have overnight in San Francisco, and overnight in Los Angeles.
